name: Wide-Grip Upright Row
movementPattern: Vertical pull - shoulder abduction and elbow flexion
grip: Wide pronated (overhand) grip, approximately 1.5 times shoulder width.
description: Stand upright and pull a barbell vertically to mid-chest height using a wide overhand grip, leading with the elbows flared outward to emphasize the lateral deltoids while minimizing shoulder impingement.
setup: Stand tall with feet hip-width apart and knees softly unlocked.
Grip the barbell with an overhand grip approximately 1.5 times shoulder width.
Let the bar hang at arms length across the upper thighs, shoulders retracted and depressed.
instructions: Pull the barbell upward along the torso by flaring elbows upward and outward.
Continue lifting until elbows reach shoulder height and the bar reaches mid-chest level.
Ensure hands remain below the level of the elbows at the apex of the pull.
Lower the barbell under control back to the starting hang position.
cues: Stand tall without swinging the hips.
commonMistakes: Using a narrow grip which causes internal shoulder impingement.
Pulling the bar too high to the chin, forcing wrists above elbows.
Using excessive body momentum or hip thrusting to lift the weight.

logging.example: Bar (20 kg) plus 20 kg plates: record 40 kg total barbell mass.
logging.note: Record total combined mass of the barbell and loaded plates.

variantNote: Wide-grip barbell variation (hands approx. 1.5x shoulder width). Minimizes subacromial impingement compared to narrow-grip upright rows.
